name: layer_main_latched
description: Frozen reference behaviour: the mesh EDIT TARGET is latched, not derived from the item selection. It tracks the last-selected MESH and is untouched by selecting a non-mesh item. So the transform set and the edit target are two different things — which is exactly how selecting only a reference-image item avoids dragging the mesh.
source: Frozen reference capture (headless, scripted): a two-mesh scene plus one non-mesh item, six selection steps, reading the edit target's identity after each.

provenance.harness: private headless capture harness (case script + per-case result JSON live in the private tree)
provenance.notes: A ONE-mesh scene cannot answer this — the edit target would have only one possible non-empty value, so 'it never changed' would be equally consistent with latched and with constant. Two earlier runs were exactly that and are not evidence on their own; only the two-mesh run below is. An independent second line of evidence was obtained in the same session: with ONLY the non-mesh item selected, an auto-fit operation on it fitted to the UNSELECTED mesh's bounds.

rows.role: CONTROL — the edit target DID move when a different mesh was selected, so the read is live. Without this row every later 'it did not move' is worthless: an inert read predicts the same thing.
latched — selecting a non-mesh item leaves the edit target where the last mesh selection put it
rows.set_note: TASK 0668: the reference's set — the non-mesh item ALONE — is representable now, so this row asserts it. It is the parity 0668 bought, and it is what keeps the divergence row below non-vacuous: a fixture whose every assertion is 'we differ' passes just as well when the channel is broken.

rows.role: re-arm, so step 5 latches onto a DIFFERENT mesh than step 3 did
latched again, and to the other mesh — so the value follows the last mesh selection rather than being pinned to one particular layer
rows.set_note: TASK 0668: the reference's set — the non-mesh item ALONE — is representable now, so this row asserts it. It is the parity 0668 bought, and it is what keeps the divergence row below non-vacuous: a fixture whose every assertion is 'we differ' passes just as well when the channel is broken.

rows.role: a mixed selection resolves to the mesh. The ONLY row that exercises an ADD (every other row is an exclusive set), and the only one whose selected SET the reference and vibe3d agree on — so it is where an `add` that no-ops on a non-mesh item, or that evicts the mesh already in the set, is caught.

control_row_is_load_bearing: Step 2 is why this fixture asserts anything. Every other row reports that the edit target did NOT follow the selection; a broken or constant read reports that too. Step 2 is the only row where the two predictions differ.
step_6_is_not_a_repeat: Step 6's edit-target column alone cannot fail: it opens with `set mesh A`, which already forces the edit target to mesh A, so an `add` that does nothing reads the right answer. What makes the row discriminating is the pair of columns beside it — the item-selection FOCUS must have moved onto the added non-mesh item, and the selected SET must be exactly the two items named. Steps 1, 2 and 4 cannot substitute: they never issue an `add` at all, and steps 3 and 5 reach the non-mesh item through an exclusive `set`, a different path.

corroboration.what: auto-fit on the non-mesh item, with only that item selected
corroboration.result: it fitted to the UNSELECTED mesh's bounds
corroboration.detail: the item went from unit scale to (3,3,1) and from the origin to (5,0,1.5), matching the mesh that was sitting at position (5,0,0) with scale (3,3,3)
corroboration.why_it_corroborates: a second, independent consumer of the edit target reached the same latched mesh

not_answered.what: whether a non-mesh item is pickable in the viewport
not_answered.why: The item's image link defaults to none, so it draws nothing and a click cannot reach it. The control leg — forcing it selectable — selected nothing on a centre click, which proves the rig could not deliver a click to it at all; the default leg's 'nothing was selected' would therefore have been vacuous. Blocked, not negative.

classification.was: This fixture has now held three verdicts, and the sequence is the record of how the model was arrived at. "match" before task 0668: vibe3d reproduced the edit-target column row for row and differed only in the selected SET on steps 3 and 5, which its ≥¹1-selected invariant could not hold. "mixed" after 0668, which TRADED the two halves — it made the exclusive select exclusive for every kind, so the reference's set became reproducible, and paid for it by dropping the edit target the reference keeps. "match" again now: task 0670 READ the mechanism instead of inferring it and there was never a trade to make. Per selection type the reference keeps two lists, the current selection and a cache of recently deselected elements, bucketed by item type; the foreground list walks both and the edit target is that walk's head. Selecting a non-mesh item flushes only its own bucket, so the mesh stays in the mesh one — non-zero selection state, therefore foreground, therefore still the target — while the SELECTED set is the non-mesh item alone. Both columns, one mechanism.

edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.reference: the edit target stays LATCHED on the last-selected mesh
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.vibe3d: there is no edit target at all (`active` reports -1)
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.why: WHAT IS MEASURED, and it is only this: on an exclusive select of a non-mesh item the reference's selected set is that item ALONE, and its edit target stays on the last-selected mesh. vibe3d derives foreground from the selection (`foreground(l) == visible && selected`), so a target that is not selected would draw as BACKGROUND — dimmed and read-only — while the toolpipe wrote to it. Task 0654 examined that state and declared it unrepresentable, so vibe3d has two answers available and the reference's reading is not among them: keep the mesh SELECTED (pre-0668, the defect the owner reported) or drop the target (0668).
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.read_by: 0670 — the task that established the mechanism by READING the reference's own declarations and shipped code. 0671 is the task that landed it here, and is therefore what `closed_by` names; the reading is where the model came from and is cited separately so neither can be looked up in place of the other.
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.corroboration_still_stands: The auto-fit reading recorded under `corroboration` is a second, independent OBSERVATION of the reference reaching the same mesh — evidence for the behaviour, not for any particular mechanism behind it. It is unaffected by this marker and is a row task 0670's answer has to account for.
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.closed_by_what: Task 0670 established what the reference actually does by READING; task 0671 implemented it. This fixture was the acceptance test and the marker retired itself the day rows 3 and 5 agreed — the test demanded the edit, it was not volunteered.
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.accepted_cost: PAID OFF. While the divergence was open, creating an image plane left NO edit target, and with task 0669 merged that drew the primitive buttons grey until a mesh was selected again — accepted by the owner on 2026-08-10. Task 0671 removes the cost rather than tolerating it: the mesh stays latched, so the buttons stay live.
edit_target_unlatches_on_nonmesh_exclusi.inferred_not_read: The usual EXPLANATION — that the reference's edit target is a latched pointer living outside the item selection — was an INFERENCE from the rows above, and it was WRONG IN MECHANISM even though it fits every row here. There is no second variable: selectedness is three-valued (current / recently-deselected / neither), the deselect cache is bucketed by item type, and the target is the head of a walk over both lists. The two constructions agree on every row of this fixture and diverge immediately outside it — on undo, on delete, on multi-select order, on a second deselect — which is exactly why the mechanism had to be read rather than fitted. Kept here as a caution: a model that reproduces a frozen fixture is not thereby the right model.

classification.live_parity_note: ALL SIX rows are now asserted against the reference, edit target and selected set alike. While the marker was open this list held 1, 2, 4 and 6 — the rows that demonstrated the channel could still AGREE, which is what stopped the two marked rows being vacuous. That job is done; the CONTROL (row 2) and the only `add` row (row 6) still carry it, and rows 3 and 5 have joined them rather than replaced them.
